title: Xenopus tadpoles with only a tail eye can see through it

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Xenopus tadpoles with only a tail eye can see through it

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Xenopus laevis tadpoles produced with no primary eyes and a single eye on the tail can see out of the ectopic eye, which can connect to the spinal cord, showing that a frog's cellular hardware can adapt within one generation to a radical reconfiguration of its visual system.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Beyond standard model organisms: stories of plasticity and change

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Tadpoles of the frog Xenopus laevis can be produced with no primary eyes, but one eye on their tails; these animals can see out of an ectopic eye, which can connect to the spinal cord (Blackiston and Levin 2013).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Beyond standard model organisms: stories of plasticity and change”. Scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles with transplanted ectopic eyes (author's lab, Blackiston and Levin 2013)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The visual-performance claim is concrete and has informative controls. Public records may resolve the experimental outcome, but mechanism and the broader adaptation framing are less fully tested.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reanalyze blinded visual-conditioning trials for eyeless tadpoles bearing one tail eye against eyeless and normal-eye controls, and relate performance to graft innervation. Successful learning specific to visual cues confirms function through the ectopic eye.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
One-generation adaptation is inferred from the preparation rather than directly measured.

Nonvisual light responses require exclusion.

Raw trial data and connectivity images may not be jointly available.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.82
operationalizability: 0.95
data existence: 0.58
data adequacy: 0.52
analysis feasibility: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is the same preparation as the behavioural tail-eye result, with a narrower endpoint: vision and a spinal connection. The experimental paper publishes those outcomes for this scope. They can be checked against the described controls and cannot be recomputed from an open trial file.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In Xenopus tadpoles with no primary eyes and one tail eye, score visually guided learning and trace axons from that eye. Learning that requires the tail eye, with axons entering the spinal cord, would support seeing through the ectopic eye; chance performance, or learning that remains after the tail eye is removed, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Published performance is a summary, not trial-level choices.

Extraocular photoreception is the main rival and has to be read off the paper's controls.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.45
